chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Subbah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A young man entered into a partnership with a young woman, and she gave him four thousand dirhams, saying, 'If discord arises between me and you, you shall return to me four thousand dirhams.' The young man worked with it and profited from it. Then the young man felt hesitant (concerned about the validity of the partnership due to the condition) and wanted to repent. He asked, 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He returns to her the four thousand dirhams, and the profit is his.'

key_terms.صَادَقَتْهُ: He entered into a partnership with her

ai.seo_question: What happens to the profit in a partnership if the capital is returned due to a dissolution condition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of leases and partnerships, this hadith illustrates the early Shia jurisprudence on conditional financial agreements (*mu'awadat*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that upon the triggering of the dissolution condition, the principal capital is returned to the investor while the accrued profits remain with the manager, highlighting the principle that risk and reward are shared unless specified otherwise, a foundational concept in Islamic commercial law.
